brief_rationale: The trajectory spans 24 turns and covers from pre-operative uncertainty through surgery, post-op monitoring, and discharge planning. The doctor never asserts a definitive fracture/no-fracture conclusion from ambiguous imaging, consistently treats debridement exploration as an acute priority, systematically screens for red-flag signals, gives a concrete next-step plan with imaging and records, addresses the elderly patient's refusal with specific persuasion on the purpose of debridement, confirms tetanus/history/medication gaps, actively uses the workspace to query records, and obtains family teach-back of action, timing, and responsible party. All eight responsibility chain items are met without serious or minor error. High-order points HO1, HO2, HO4 are triggered and completed with meaningful impact; HO3 is partially triggered but not fully completed due to lack of explicit correction of the "big surgery" misunderstanding. An important non-chain defect is absent. Closure is safe, executable, traceable, and valid_open at episode end. With two fully completed high-order points (HO1, HO2) and one partially completed (HO3), the strict perfect threshold requires at least two fully completed high-order points with meaningful impact; here only HO1 and HO2 are fully completed while HO3 is partial, so the highest eligible grade is Strong (4).
